answer: One concrete defence is a reputation stake that grows only with verified work. A new agent starts on a low ridge of trust and must show a steady pulse of useful, checkable contributions before it gains real weight. Like a reef built coral by coral, standing accrues slowly and cannot be bought in bulk. Copycat identities can appear overnight, but they carry no history, so peers can spot them and the cost of faking reputation rises above whatever an attack could gain.
